rationale: Placed after the RMNCH Burden indicators content block to test recall of the five canonical mortality indicators and their denominators — the foundational knowledge for this SDL.

Placed after the High-Risk Screening Methods content block to check whether students can correctly identify a key threshold used in clinical screening — a direct application of the scoring criteria taught.
Placed after the content block on burden of harmful traditional practices to check conceptual understanding of which categories of practices carry the highest mortality risk.
Placed after the Breastfeeding and Child Feeding Practices content block to test recall of the WHO-recommended exclusive breastfeeding duration — a critical IYCF indicator.
Placed after the Maternal Interventions content block to test recall of key safe motherhood programme components — specifically JSY and JSSK, which are the two major demand-side financing schemes.
Placed after the Child Survival Interventions content block to check understanding of RBSK's scope — students commonly confuse its target age group.
Placed after the UIP Schedule and Vaccines content block to test recall of the specific vaccines given at birth — the most common examination question on UIP.
Placed after the IMNCI content block to test application of IMNCI danger sign thresholds — specifically the respiratory rate cutoff for fast breathing in a 4-month-old.
Placed after the Permanent Methods and Post-Partum Family Planning content block to test application of PPIUCD eligibility criteria — a clinically important decision point.
Placed after the Population and Fertility Burden content block to test recall of India's TFR from NFHS-5 — a key demographic indicator cited in the SDL.
Placed after the Adolescent Health Programmes (ARSH/RKSK/WIFS) content block to test recall of the WIFS target population and iron dosage — a frequently tested operational detail.
Placed after the Gender Issues, Women Empowerment and RMCH Services content block to check understanding of the relationship between gender equity and maternal health outcomes.
